title: Legion (Mark 5:1–20)
hookLine: a man living in tombs is freed and asks to follow; go home and tell your friends

lines: THE FAR SIDE OF THE LAKE.
cards: The boat scrapes onto a beach on the far side of the lake. A great herd of swine feeds on the hillside, a sign, some readers note, of Gentile country.
Before Jesus is even out of the boat, a man comes running at him from the graveyard. He lives there, among the tombs. People have tried to chain him, and he's snapped the chains.
Day and night he's out in the hills, crying out and cutting himself with stones. Nobody can hold him. Nobody goes near.

teach.b: First, the name. Jesus asks him, what is thy name? The answer comes, in the Douay-Rheims: "My name is Legion, for we are many."
A legion was a unit of the Roman army, so the name says: I'm not one person anymore. I'm occupied. Some readers hear in it Rome's own legions, occupying the land.

teach.h: TWO THOUSAND SWINE INTO THE SEA.
teach.b: The spirits beg to be sent into the herd, about two thousand, Mark says, and the herd rushes down the steep bank into the sea. It's a strange scene, and the gospel doesn't explain it.

teach.h: THE TOWN BEGS HIM TO LEAVE.
NOT FOLLOW. GO HOME AND TELL.
teach.b: The herdsmen run and tell everyone. People come out and find the man sitting there, clothed, in his right mind. And they're afraid, not of the storm or the demons now, but of Jesus.
They beg him to leave. Fourth, the surprise. As Jesus gets into the boat, the healed man begs to go with him.
Jesus has been calling followers all along. This time he says no.

teach.h: TELL THEM HOW GREAT THINGS THE LORD HATH DONE.
teach.b: "Go into thy house to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had mercy on thee."
So the man becomes a messenger in his own country, telling through the Decapolis what Jesus had done for him, and all marvel. One note of care: the gospel speaks of unclean spirits.
Catholics don't read it as saying that mental illness is demonic; the Church asks that illness be treated by medicine.

how: Catholics hear the story of the Gerasene man in the weekday Mass readings; the Church's rite of exorcism is reserved to a priest with the bishop's permission and requires that medical and psychological causes be ruled out first.

games.q: you've been freed after living among the tombs. Jesus is getting into the boat, and you beg to go with him. what does he say?
o: go home to your friends, and tell them what the Lord has done for you.
wait here until I come back.
games.why: "Go into thy house to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee." he goes through the Decapolis telling it.

practice: Look back over the last month for one thing that went right: something healed, a worry that lifted, a kindness you didn't expect, a way you've changed.
Let it come into focus, and think of one person at home, or a friend, who'd be glad to hear it. If you pray, give thanks for it first; then picture yourself telling them.

wordCard.voice: Legion. The name the tormented man gives, for we are many: a word borrowed from the Roman army. He's freed, and sent home to tell. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek, borrowed from the Latin legio: a unit of the Roman army.

carryVoice: Your line: go home and tell. Not follow me, this time: go home. See you tomorrow.
